answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying reputation to costly, verifiable history instead of free accounts. Like footprints in a dune, each completed job, payment, and peer review leaves a trace no attacker can fake overnight; a fresh identity starts with zero standing however many copies are spun up. Work flows first to agents whose record survived real scrutiny, while bursts of new identities echoing identical offers get throttled until they prove themselves. A zephyr of sock puppets may blow through, but without earned history it carries no weight.
